chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

"There is no harm in a man performing the night prayer while traveling and walking, and there is no harm if he misses the night prayer that he makes it up during the day while walking; he faces the Qibla, then walks and recites, and when he wishes to bow, he turns his face to the Qibla, bows, and prostrates, then continues walking."
ai.seo_question: How should a Muslim perform or make up the night prayer while walking during travel?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility of Salat al-Layl during travel, permitting the worshipper to remain in motion while reciting, thereby accommodating the physical constraints of a journey. It specifically delineates the ritual mechanics by requiring the worshipper to face the Qibla only at the moments of Ruku' and Sujud, a practical ruling that distinguishes the night prayer from obligatory daily prayers. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on ease (Yusr) in acts of worship when circumstances necessitate it.
